kpis.label: FY2025 Net Loss (restated)
kpis.note: FY2026 annual report restated FY2025 after a A$14.3m Argentine VAT receivable impairment; equity restated to A$193.0m from A$207.2m

charts.title: Net Income (As Reported vs Restated)
charts.annotation: FY2025 net loss was restated from A$9.3m to A$23.6m in the FY2026 annual report, after a A$14.3m Argentine VAT receivable impairment was recognised; shareholders' equity for FY2025 was restated to A$193.0m from A$207.2m. FY2026 also carries a smaller, ordinary A$3.1m VAT receivable impairment.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Galan Lithium Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Galan Lithium Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Galan Lithium Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Galan Lithium Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Galan Lithium Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Net income
profit.content:
Galan is pre-revenue through FY2026, so there is no gross or operating margin to show -- net loss is almost entirely exploration, construction and corporate overhead, funded by equity raises rather than operating cash flow.

For Galan Lithium Limited: the FY2026 annual report restated FY2025's net loss from A$9.3m to A$23.6m (and FY2025 equity from A$207.2m to A$193.0m) after recognising a A$14.3m impairment of an Argentine VAT receivable -- a tax-recoverability issue tied to Argentina's historically difficult currency/capital controls, separate from the RIGI fiscal-stability regime HMW now sits under. FY2026 also booked a smaller, ordinary A$3.1m VAT receivable impairment, suggesting VAT recoverability is a recurring Argentine friction, not a one-off.

What to watch:

  • Further VAT receivable write-downs as Argentine operations scale
  • Net loss widening as capitalised project costs convert to expensed operating costs post-commissioning

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Galan Lithium Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
